question: The rigid outer covering present outside the plasma membrane in plants is called the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**cell wall**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The cell wall is a rigid layer that is found outside the plasma membrane in plant cells, bacteria, fungi, and some algae.
 
• In plants, the cell wall is primarily composed of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin.
 
• The cell wall provides structural support and protection, and it also acts as a filtering mechanism.
 
• It is crucial for maintaining the shape of the plant cell and preventing excessive water intake through osmosis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plasma Membrane:**

 
 
• A selectively permeable membrane that regulates the entry and exit of substances in and out of the cell.
 
• Composed of a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins.
 
 
 
• **Cell Envelope:**
 
 
• In bacteria, the cell envelope includes the plasma membrane, cell wall, and sometimes an outer membrane.
 
• Provides structural integrity and protection from environmental stress.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Membrane:**
 
 
• A double membrane that encloses the nucleus in eukaryotic cells.
 
• Contains nuclear pores that allow the transport of molecules between the nucleus and cytoplasm.
 
 
 
• **Composition of Plant Cell Walls:**
 
 
• Primary Cell Wall: Thin and flexible, made of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin.
 
• Secondary Cell Wall: Thicker and more rigid, contains lignin in addition to cellulose and hemicellulose.
